submission.justification: Module-D1 has the highest light yield (38 PE/MeV at 20% coverage) but fails the robustness requirement: 30% of modules cracked after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K), against a limit of 5%, and the modules cannot be replaced after the cryostat is filled. Module-D2 is robust (0.5% failure) but has the lowest yield (18 PE/MeV at 20%). Module-D3 passes the thermal test with 2% failure and gives 27 PE/MeV at 20%. Using the stated coverage^0.8 scaling, D3 at 30% coverage gives about 27 x 1.5^0.8 = ~37 PE/MeV, the highest light yield among the robust options. 30% is the upper limit of the allowed range and is within the feedthrough capacity noted in the 2026-01-20 meeting notes. Caveats: the 37 PE/MeV figure is an extrapolation from a 2025 simulation at 20% coverage, not a direct simulation at 30%. The 2% D3 failure rate comes from 40 modules, so it has limited statistics. The cold electronics are validated for D3.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D3 (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout) is listed in candidate_specs.md.

requirements.requirement: Robustness: modules inaccessible after cryostat fill (at most 5% failures after 20 thermal cycles)
requirements.evidence: thermal_cycling_tests.md: Module-D3 failed 2% (batch of 40) after 20 cycles between 300 K and 87 K. D1 failed 30% and was excluded.
Recommended coverage 30%, the upper bound; feedthroughs are sufficient for up to 30% per meeting notes 2026-01-20.

Among robust designs, D3 gives the highest yield. At 20% it gives 27 PE/MeV vs 18 for D2. Extrapolated to 30% with coverage^0.8 scaling it gives ~37 PE/MeV. This is an extrapolation, not a direct 30% simulation. D1 (38 PE/MeV at 20%, ~53 extrapolated) would be higher but is not robust enough.
electronics.md: cold amplifiers validated for every candidate design, including D3.
